about: In-scope rule for every binary group. scripts/gen-scope.py turns this file into the binaries and scope sections of tools/config/inventory-config.json; evidence/inventory/scope.tsv reports it. 'in' puts every function of the group in scope, 'narrow' only the functions whose names start with a prefix of narrow_prefixes, 'out' none. Out of scope means not yet: the inventory keeps listing the rows. 'keep' lists routines that sit in an out or narrow group but that the inventory scan finds reaching a register window: the run refuses to exclude them, so scripts/gen-scope.py gives each binary its glob names a rule that leaves them in scope.

groups.reason: The linked kernels, in full: the hardware-facing and boot-critical subsystems (PROM interface and KLCONFIG, hardware graph, interrupts, NUMA and memory initialisation, node and router topology, the I/O attach framework, debug and panic entry points) and the generic kernel (processes, scheduler, virtual memory, file systems, networking, IPC, system calls).
Platform core and debugger objects: the hardware-facing and generic code in them, in full.
Objects that exist only for the NUMA, hardware-graph, crossbar, bridge, node-board and attach machinery of the in-scope subsystems.

DM2 and DIVO video option software, read for the DM2 contract and not part of the base platform. Listed before kernel-other-objects so their platform boot objects leave the in-scope set; their functions are out of scope for now, not excluded.
Every other kernel object of the platform boot directories: file systems, networking, STREAMS, NFS and RPC, CXFS stubs, scheduler and virtual memory in os.a, other drivers.

Base user-space daemons and commands of the installed 6.5.30 and 6.5.22 systems: hardware inventory and configuration, the controller and power-management tools, NFS, RPC and CacheFS services, the cluster daemons, the XFS tools and the commands that the open questions name (checkpoint and restart, cpusets and miser, the IP filter daemon, the autofs daemons, the CD-ROM and SCSI control tools). Listed so the inventory counts them; their functions are out of scope for now, not excluded.

The runtime loader and the shared libraries of the installed 6.5.30 and 6.5.22 systems that the open questions name: the loader in the three ABIs, the C and maths libraries in their MIPS III and MIPS IV builds, the thread, unwinder and C++ support libraries, the X11 and XInput client libraries, the audio library and the libraries of the checkpoint, cpuset, data-placement and counter commands. Listed so the inventory counts them; their functions are out of scope for now, not excluded.

The two X server builds of the 6.5.30 and 6.5.22 media (the generic one an Octane or Onyx2 runs, and the Indigo2 NG1 build) and two commands outside the base directories, the performance-counter and job-limit tools. Listed so the inventory counts them; their functions are out of scope for now, not excluded.

selector_scope.reason: A syssgi selector is in scope when the first routine its code calls matches narrow_prefixes, the rule of the kernel image. first_call is a heuristic (blank when the code branches before calling anything), so a blank selector is out of scope for now, not excluded.
